    Live trust policy and claims

    ATEP is an open protocol. ATEP-R is its robotics profile (spec Draft 07, section 17). AIRAD LABS stewards the protocol. This page needs no network after it loads.

    What is real and what is simulated. Real: every key, attestation, revocation list and envelope, every signature, encryption, verification and decryption, including the error codes and steps shown, all done by the reference Rust crate compiled to WebAssembly. Simulated: the map, unit movement, battery values, the scripted timeline, the clock, the moment the controller goes offline, and the certified status of Units 2 and 4, so no real certification is implied. When the controller is offline, units verify each other with the certificates and revocation lists they saved earlier; a revocation published meanwhile cannot reach them until the controller is back. This is an illustration of the robotics profile, not a product.
